axis: wearing enough to tire → weighing down hard enough to smother

members.tone: The plainest name for the condition itself, sadness or trouble felt as weight from inside, where *burdensome* describes the load from outside.
Puts the difficulty in the thing rather than the bearer: a load fixed on you that has to be carried, not merely a strain that tires.
The formal member, and the heaviest-sounding of the three, where *taxing* keeps the same complaint everyday.
Leans on the wearing half of the sense, draining strength steadily rather than crushing, the lightest of the three.
The plain, full-strength member of the group, naming real hurt and not merely unease.
The stiffer, more formal shape of *distressing*, with the same weight of hurt behind it.
Aimed at composure rather than comfort, it unsettles and goes on unsettling, where *distressing* simply hurts.
The mildest and most formal here, ruffling the mind where *disturbing* unseats it.
Quiet and persistent, a worry that nags at you instead of striking, understated beside *distressing*.
Treats the power to cause anxiety as a standing property of the thing, where *worrying* reports what it is doing now.
Keeps to the worry-and-anxiety end of the sense, unease rather than the hurt *distressing* names.
The most physical word in the family, heaviness and weariness fused into dead metal, dull and unliftable.
The flattest member, recording that the weight has been put on without making the weariness of it felt as *leaden* does.
The strongest weight here, pressing on the senses as much as on the spirit and leaving no room to breathe.
Grave rather than smothering, the weight registering as anxiety carried, where *oppressive* closes in.
